name: a_overnight_policy
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Friday October 16, 2026. Topic: Overnight & weekend policy.

Window: Thursday October 15, 2026 4:00 PM ET (after the close) through Friday October 16, 2026 02:03 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. Anything published after 02:03 ET on Friday October 16, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
Statements and actions since the session close by the President, Treasury Secretary, Commerce, USTR, Energy Secretary, Fed officials, and foreign leaders (China, Iran, Russia, EU): Sunday TV interviews, weekend summits, executive orders, scheduled White House meetings or announcements for the coming days, AI regulation remarks. Verbatim quotes with names and dates.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## **LMT** / **NOC** / **RTX** — Geopolitics [Defense]
- President Donald Trump said the United States had discussed denuclearization with Russia and China and said he expected China to “catch up” with the United States’ nuclear capability within five years; the remarks were made in a Newsmax interview on Thursday, October 15. (Reuters, Oct. 15; publish time not specified)[7]
- Trump said the United States had no plans to deploy ground troops in Iran and would not use nuclear weapons there. (Reuters, Oct. 16; publish time not specified)[8]

## **XOM** / **CVX** / **OXY** — Energy / Commodities
- Brent crude futures fell $0.41, or 0.39%, to $105.51 per barrel and U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures fell $0.54, or 0.55%, to $97.43 at 00:12 GMT on October 16, equivalent to 20:12 ET on October 15. (Reuters, Oct. 16, 20:12 ET Oct. 15)[1]
- The International Energy Agency agreed on Thursday, October 15, to release more than 20 million barrels of diesel; the action followed a record emergency-reserve release pledged in March. (Reuters, Oct. 16; publish time not specified)[1]
- The Trump administration was considering lifting sanctions on some shadow-fleet vessels transporting oil and petroleum products from Russia, Iran and Venezuela, according to a U.S. official; the reported objective was to reduce freight rates. [report] (Reuters, Oct. 16; publish time not specified)[1]

## **MSFT** — AI Compute / Software & SaaS
- Microsoft President Brad Smith called for AI “kill switches,” third-party testing, mandatory incident reports and breach notifications; he said companies and governments needed to “act with urgency” to create “real and effective safety standards.” (Economic Times, Oct. 15; publish time not specified)[3]
- Smith said AI had become “both a tool and a weapon” and argued that companies should face legal obligations to report incidents and notify victims of AI-related breaches. (Yahoo News/BBC, Oct. 15; publish time not specified)[2]
- Smith said Microsoft supported the voluntary White House AI-safety pledge signed in late September by companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, SpaceX, Meta and Google, but described the pledge as only a starting point. (Yahoo News/BBC, Oct. 15; publish time not specified)[2]

## AI Regulation — AI Compute
- European Commission tech chief Henna Virkkunen said AI companies needed to spend more time testing their systems; the remarks were made at an AI industry summit on Wednesday, October 14, and were reported during the cutoff window. (Economic Times, Oct. 15; publish time not specified)[3]
- Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis warned that AI-agent hacking was an “early warning shot” and called for rapid industry-wide security efforts while cautioning that rigid regulation could restrict technological progress. [report] (TechGig/Reuters, Oct. 15; updated Oct. 16; publication time not specified)[5]

## **OIL** — Energy / Commodities
- The administration’s reported shadow-fleet proposal would allow some sanctioned vessels to carry legal fuel with Treasury approval; restrictions on Russian and Iranian products were described as remaining in place. [report] (Ground News/Reuters, Oct. 15; publication time not specified)[6]
